entries.in_this_app: Not shown directly, but recessions show up as big drawdowns on long charts.

faq.question: Is this a prediction? Will the price really go there?
faq.answer: No. Nothing in this app predicts the future, and nobody can reliably predict markets. The simulations show a range of possibilities based on how the stock behaved in the past, and the indicators describe what has already happened. Real prices can move outside any range, because of news, results or events no model can see.

faq.question: Should I buy this stock? Is it a good investment?
faq.answer: I can't give buy or sell advice. This is an educational project, not investment advice. I can explain what the numbers in the app mean so you can understand the stock better. For real investment decisions, do your own research and consider speaking to a SEBI-registered investment adviser.

faq.question: Is the money real? Can I lose money here?
faq.answer: No real money is involved. Paper trading uses virtual money only. Prices are real market prices, but nothing is actually bought or sold, so you can't win or lose real money here.

faq.question: Where does the data come from? Why is the price different from my broker?
faq.answer: Prices and financial data come from Yahoo Finance, a free source. It can be delayed or occasionally incomplete, especially for Indian company financials. Your broker's prices are the official live ones, so trust those for real trading.

faq.question: How is my portfolio saved? Can others see it?
faq.answer: Your paper-trading portfolio is saved online under the name you chose, so you can come back as a returning user. Pick a name others are unlikely to use, since anyone who enters the same name can open that portfolio. It only contains virtual money and trades.

faq.question: How do I start over with a different amount?
faq.answer: In the Paper trading tab you can start over with a new starting amount, or add more virtual money. Since it's virtual money, you can experiment freely.

faq.question: Who made this app?
faq.answer: This app was built by Freya Shah of PreSC Commerce - B, Mayo College Girls School, for the school's annual function exhibition. It builds on a paper-trading app made by a senior last year, adding technical analysis, risk measures, simulations, strategy tests and fusion analysis based on the CMT curriculum. It was coded with the help of an AI coding tool. Tap the small 'i' at the top of the page to read more about the creator.

faq.question: What is CMT?
faq.answer: CMT stands for Chartered Market Technician, a professional designation in technical analysis awarded by the CMT Association. It has three levels covering charting, indicators, risk management, backtesting and combining technical with fundamental analysis (fusion analysis).

faq.question: What is EPAT?
faq.answer: EPAT is the Executive Programme in Algorithmic Trading, offered by QuantInsti. It teaches quantitative and algorithmic trading: statistics, programming in Python, strategy design, backtesting and risk management.

faq.question: Why did the trading rule lose to buy and hold?
faq.answer: That's common and realistic. Trading rules get in and out late, miss some of the best days while in cash, and pay costs every time they switch. Their usual benefit is a smaller worst fall, not a higher return. Beating simple buy-and-hold after costs is genuinely hard.

faq.question: Why is the chance of ending higher below 50%?
faq.answer: That percentage comes from the simulation's assumptions, not from real knowledge of the future. The simulation uses the stock's past-year average direction, so a stock that has been falling will lean towards 'lower'. Treat it as a description of the model, not a forecast.

faq.question: How do I start investing for real?
faq.answer: In India you need a demat and trading account with a SEBI-registered broker, which requires KYC (PAN, Aadhaar and bank details). Many beginners start small, learn with paper trading first, and consider diversified options like index funds. This isn't advice; consider talking to a SEBI-registered adviser.

faq.question: Can you explain more simply / in more detail?
faq.answer: Sure. Just tell me an age, like 'explain like I'm 8' or 'I'm 13', or pick a level above the chat box. Ages 1 to 10 get the simplest version, 11 to 15 get a bit more detail, and 16 and above get the full explanation. You can also tap the related-term buttons under my answers to ask about any word.

fallback: I can only answer from my notes about the terms and features in this app. Try asking something like 'What is RSI?', 'What does beta mean?' or 'Is this a prediction?'. I can't give buy or sell advice.
